newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end higher, back to setting records.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end higher, back to setting records.

text.p: Swiss shares set a closing record in the blue-chip SMI on Friday, regaining energy after a ten-day run of record highs was halted by a lower finish the day before.
The session saw many ups and downs. Some investors were cautious ahead of the weekend and because some U.S. markets would be closed on Monday for Presidents' Day, traders said.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) ended higher by 27.9 points or 0.63 percent at 4,464.2 points. The index also hit an all-time high at 4,473.5.
All-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) was up 15.09 points, or 0.53 percent, to 2,839.43 points.
Dealers said the market was upheld by firming futures, a three-year high of the U.S. dollar against the Swiss franc and Wall Street's overnight gains. Sentiment was likely to remain good, they added.
Drops in prices were regularly followed by new buying, one trader said.

UBS bearer shares saw heavy buying, ending up 16 francs to 1,293 after briefly hitting 1,300. One dealer pointed out that the shares overcame technical resistance at 1,285 francs. SBC and CS Group also firmed.
Roche certificates gained 105 francs to 12,570. "After several days of buying in Novartis, it is Roche's turn again," one dealer said. Novartis bearer shares were up seven francs to 1,747.
Alusuisse jumped 29 francs, or 2.51 percent, to 1,186, recovering from recent lows.
ABB slipped two francs to 1,828 francs. Some investors feared that ABB's 1996 figures, due on February 27, may be below expectations, a dealer said.
SMH bearers went up nine francs to 947.
